Gold, silver slide as Treasury yields surge, Fed hike concerns intensify - Kitco PM Report
items.summaryEn: (Kitco NewsWire) - Spot gold and silver prices were sharply lower in late U.S. trading Thursday, pressured by rising Treasury yields, a firm U.S. dollar and expectations for additional Federal Reserve interest rate increases. Gold extended its decline below $3,900.00 an ounce as investors reassessed the outlook for restrictive monetary policy, while silver suffered heavier percentage losses amid renewed concerns about industrial demand and equity-market volatility. Spot gold was trading near $3,876.40 an ounce, down $110.60, or 2.77%, while spot silver was trading near $49.930, down $1.610, or 3.13%. Thursday's U.S. economic reports highlighted the competing pressures of resilient employment conditions and weakening interest-rate-sensitive sectors. Initial jobless claims increased to 200,000 in the week ended Nov. 7, compared with expectations near 195,000, but remained consistent with relatively limited layoffs. October existing-home sales fell 5.5% to a seasonally adjusted annual rate of 3.75 million, the weakest pace since August 2010, as mortgage rates above 7% restrained demand. The housing figures followed Tuesday's stronger-than-expected consumer inflation report, which showed headline prices rising 0.4% and core prices increasing 0.3% in October. Together with last week's stronger employment report, the data indicate that elevated borrowing costs are restricting housing activity without yet producing sufficient relief from inflation. Market positioning remained firmly focused on additional Federal Reserve tightening. Late-session futures assessments indicated approximately an 85% probability of a 25-basis-point increase at the Dec. 8-9 meeting and a 15% probability of a 50-basis-point move. Treasury yields rose sharply, with the benchmark 10-year yield reaching approximately 5.102% and the two-year yield climbing to 4.862%, reflecting expectations that monetary policy may remain restrictive for longer. The dollar also remained strong, compounding pressure on gold and silver. Friday's October producer price index, scheduled for release at 8:30 a.m. EST, is the next major inflation test. Another upside surprise could reinforce expectations for aggressive tightening, while softer producer prices could provide some relief to Treasury yields and precious metals.

items.titleEn: The gold is all there! Tether Gold releases KPMG audit of its reserves
items.summaryEn: (Kitco News) - Analysts have noted that the biggest hurdle to the adoption of tokenized gold remains trust; investors have to trust that tokens are backed by secure physical gold. The world’s biggest gold-backed token has announced a significant step toward establishing that trust. Tether, the world’s largest digital asset firm, announced Thursday that KPMG U.S. has completed an independent audit of the financial statements of Tether Gold (XAU₮) for the year ended December 31, 2025. “The audited statements show XAU₮ fully backed by allocated physical gold ,” the company said in the report.
